*Kusalattika, Parittārammaṇattika* is an Abhidhamma text situated in the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final book of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. As reflected in its title, the section examines the matrix of conditional relations (*paccaya*) by coordinating the *Kusalattika* (the triad of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states) with the *Parittārammaṇattika* (the triad of states with limited or minor objects) [SuttaCentral].

No parallel versions in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan traditions are recorded in SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Textual reuse within the Pali canon is substantial due to the formulaic and combinatorial nature of the *Paṭṭhāna*. DharmaNexus identifies 91 matching passages distributed across 30 other Pali texts, exclusively within the *Paṭṭhāna* itself [DharmaNexus]. The most significant overlaps occur in segments §1.1–3.1, which share extensive formulaic phrasings with texts such as *Kusalattika, Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 22.6), *Kusalattika, Cūḷantaraduka* (Patthana 22.5), *Kusalattika, Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 16.25), and a structurally related treatment in *Kusalattika, Parittārammaṇattika* (Patthana 17.12) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
